explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Numbers 33:2 says, "At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey." Moses, Israel's leader, isn't scribbling for fun here. He's writing down every stop because the LORD told him to. Not a bad assignment, since somebody has to remember all those tent stakes.

Good guess, since Aaron is right there. Numbers 33:1 says the Israelites came out under the leadership of Moses and Aaron. But the writing order comes from somewhere higher. Verse 2 says, "At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey." Aaron, Moses' brother and Israel's priest, is on the trip, but the command came from the LORD.

I get why you'd think a committee did it. Nobody likes a trip with no group chat. But the text names one writer and one source. Numbers 33:2 says, "At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey." The tribal leaders aren't mentioned in that verse.

explanations.answer: Defiantly in full view of the Egyptians
explanations.explanation: Right on, friend. Numbers 33:3 says they "marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians." No tiptoeing and no sneaking. I spent years sneaking out of a drawer in my dreams, and these folks just WALKED out the front. I admire that.

explanations.answer: Quietly while nobody was watching them
explanations.explanation: Nope, this one's the opposite. Numbers 33:3 says they marched out "in full view of all the Egyptians." Everybody could see them go. Quiet and unseen would be a very different exit.

explanations.answer: In a hurry before the sun came up
explanations.explanation: I can see why you'd say that, since it sounds like a getaway. But this passage doesn't mention a rush or the hour. It says they "marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians" (Numbers 33:3). The word is defiantly, not hurriedly.

Yes, baker. The Egyptians were burying "all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them" (Numbers 33:4). It's a heavy picture. I think this part of the story hurts, and it deserves a quiet moment before we move on.

Soldiers makes sense for a big story like this one. But Numbers 33:4 names who was being buried: "all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them." That's the word that fits the blank. It's a heavy verse, so I'll just say it plainly.

Elders is a fair guess, but it's not what the verse says. Numbers 33:4 says the Egyptians were burying "all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them." That's a heavy moment, and the text keeps it simple. I think the right move is to read it slowly.

True, baker. Numbers 33:4 says "the LORD had executed judgment against their gods." Egypt had plenty of gods, and the LORD dealt with them too. The verse puts it right next to the striking down of the firstborn.

This one's true, so no worries on the guess. Numbers 33:4 says the Egyptians were burying their firstborn, "for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods." So there were two things going on at once. The firstborn were struck down, and judgment came against Egypt's gods.

That's the one. Numbers 33:8 says they "crossed through the sea, into the wilderness." Through it, friend. I once got stuck behind a stack of takeout menus, and these folks walked through a whole SEA.
Going around sounds like the sensible route. But Numbers 33:8 says they "crossed through the sea, into the wilderness." Through, not around. That's the part you'd want to tell your friends.

Heading back would be a lot of walking for nothing. The text goes a different way. Numbers 33:8 says they "crossed through the sea, into the wilderness." Succoth was already behind them, back in verse 5.

Not this time, baker. Numbers 33:14 says they camped at Rephidim, "where there was no water for the people to drink." Remember Elim, with its twelve springs? Rephidim was the opposite. Plenty of water would have been a nice surprise, but the verse says none.

Correct, it's false. Numbers 33:14 says they camped at Rephidim, "where there was no water for the people to drink." After Elim and its twelve springs, that's a big change. Water was the thing missing at that stop.
Yes, Mount Hor. Numbers 33:37 says they camped there, "on the outskirts of the land of Edom." Edom is the land next door. Good eye, baker.

Mount Carmel is a real mountain, but it's not in this list of stops. In Numbers 33:37, the camp after Kadesh is Mount Hor, "on the outskirts of the land of Edom." Easy to mix up when there are this many place names flying around. I'd need a map and a snack, and my only snack is a cookie.

Mount Gerizim sounds right when you're juggling this many names. It's not what the verse says, though. Numbers 33:37 says they set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, "on the outskirts of the land of Edom." Mount Hor is the answer.

True, baker. Numbers 33:38 says, "At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest climbed Mount Hor and died there." So he climbed because the LORD commanded it. This stop is a heavy one, and I think it's worth slowing down for.
This one's true, so don't sweat it. Numbers 33:38 says, "At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest climbed Mount Hor and died there." Aaron didn't just wander up there. The command came from the LORD.

That's right, friend. Numbers 33:38 says Aaron "climbed Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month." It's a sad line in the middle of a long list of places. No joke here from me. I think the right thing to do is just let it be heavy for a second.

An altar sounds like something a priest would do. But that's not what the verse says. Numbers 33:38 says Aaron "climbed Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month." It's a heavy moment, so I'll leave it at that.

Blessing the tribes fits a priest, I'll give you that. But the verse gives a different ending. Numbers 33:38 says Aaron "climbed Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month." I think this one is just sad, friend.

Yes, baker. Numbers 33:40 says the king of Arad "heard that the Israelites were coming." That's all the verse tells us. How he felt about it, the text doesn't say. I'd guess nobody in the Negev was ready for that news, but that's just me.

explanations.answer: That Aaron had died on Mount Hor
explanations.explanation: That's a fair mix-up, since Aaron's death is the verse right before. But Numbers 33:40 says the king of Arad "heard that the Israelites were coming." Aaron isn't part of what he heard. The king's news was about the Israelites on the move.

Egypt's army belongs to a much earlier part of the trip, back at the start of the list. The verse about the king has a different news story. Numbers 33:40 says he "heard that the Israelites were coming." The Canaanite king, who lived in the Negev, was hearing about Israel.

explanations.answer: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Numbers 33:48 says they "camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho." That's the last stop in the list. After all that setting out and camping, they finally reach the river.

The Wilderness of Paran is a real place, but it's not in this passage's list. After the mountains of Abarim, Numbers 33:48 says they "camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho." With this many names, I'd mix them up too. Paran just isn't on this list.

The valley of Hinnom isn't one of the stops in this chapter. Numbers 33:48 says they set out from the mountains of Abarim and "camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho." That's the answer. Nice try, friend.
